requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain what public health is. (b) Explain how Escherichia coli (E. coli), tetanus, AIDS, encephalitis, salmonellosis, Lyme disease, and coronavirus (COVID-19) are contracted. (c) Choose any four of the following diseases and explain how each one is contracted and possibly prevented: gonorrhea, West Nile virus, botulism, influenza, syphilis, hepatitis, emphysema, meningitis, herpes, or lead poisoning. (d) For all 10 diseases from 1(c), explain the type or form of the disease (viral, bacterial, environmental, toxin), any possible vectors for transmission, ways to help prevent exposure or the spread of infection, and available treatments.

pamphlet_excerpts: Immune System Antibodies: The immune system makes antibodies for each particulardisease that it meets.
Therefore Different Vaccine: Therefore, a different vaccine is neededfor each disease.
Immunizationsalso Available: Immunizationsalso are available for many other diseases that are uncommonin the United States but common in other parts of the world.
Americans Typicallyreceive: Americans typicallyreceive these immunizations when they travel out of the countryor join the armed forces.
step_by_step_procedure: Immunization Suggested Young: Immunization is suggested for very young children, withperiodic booster injections as recommended.
Antibodies Arelong-lasting: Antibodies arelong-lasting, but the protection they give may decrease withtime.
Exposure Pathogen Increase: A second exposure to a pathogen will increase the level ofantibodies a person’s body will produce.
Injection Booster Shot: So a second injection, or booster shot, often is given to help strengthen immunity.

requirements.lead_text: With your parent or guardian's and counselor's approval, do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: With your parent or guardian's and counselor's approval, do ONE of the following: (a) Visit a municipal wastewater treatment facility or a solid-waste management operation in your community. (1) Describe how the facility safely treats and disposes of sewage or solid waste. (2) Discuss your visit and what you learned with your counselor. (3) Describe how sewage and solid waste should be disposed of under wilderness camping conditions. (b) Visit a food service facility, such as a restaurant or school cafeteria. (1) Observe food preparation, handling, and storage. Learn how the facility keeps food from becoming contaminated. (2) Find out what conditions allow microorganisms to multiply in food, what can be done to help prevent them from growing and spreading, and how to kill them. (3) Discuss the importance of using a thermometer to check food temperatures. (4) Discuss your visit and what you learned with your counselor.

pamphlet_excerpts: Municipal Sewage Treatment: Municipal sewage treatment systems are designed to handlelarge volumes of sewage and liquid wastes.
Raw Sewageflows Treatment: The raw sewageflows to a treatment plant through underground pipes (mains).
Sewage Screened Allowed: Sewage is screened, allowed to settle, processed, dried, anddisinfected before disposal.
Screening Removes Objects: Screening removes objects larger than an inch or two insize that have entered sewage mains.
step_by_step_procedure: Debris Removed Then: Debris is removed and then taken to a landfillor burned.
Time Incoming Waste: By the time incoming waste reaches the sewage treatmentplant, it is mostly liquid with particles suspended in it.
Manysuspended Particles Drop: Manysuspended particles drop out of the liquid portion as thescreened sewage is allowed to settle.
Processing Treatment Done: Processing or treatment is done by two basic methods: activated sludge and trickling.

pamphlet_excerpts: World Health Organization: The World Health Organization considers tobacco use to be an epidemic becauseit kills 6 million people every year.
Substances Candamage Body: Using these substances candamage the body, lead to accompanying diseases, and causegreat numbers of injuries and accidents.
Tobacco Contains Than: Tobacco contains more than 4,000 chemical compounds, manyof which cause emphysema and cancer.
Fact Cigarette Smoking: In fact, cigarette smoking causes 87 percent of lung cancer, a rarely cured diseasewith poor survival rates.
step_by_step_procedure: Leading Causes Ofdeath: It is one of the leading causes ofdeath worldwide.
Smoking Contributes Greatly: Smoking contributes greatly to heart diseaseand stroke as well.
Smokers Began Smoking: Most smokers began smoking before they were 18 yearsold.
Nicotine Addictive: Because nicotine is one of the most addictive substancesknown to humans, young adults who start using tobacco oftenbecome hooked for life.

requirements.req_text: With your parent or guardian's and counselor's approval, do the following: (a) Do ONE of the following: (1) Visit your city, county, state, or federal public health agency. (b) After completing either 7(a)(1) or 7(a)(2), do ALL of the following: (1) Compare the four leading causes of mortality (death) in your community for any of the past five years with the four leading causes of disease in your community. Explain how the public health agency you visited is trying to reduce the mortality and morbidity rates of these leading causes of illness and death. (2) Explain the role of your health agency as it relates to the outbreak of diseases. (3) Discuss the kinds of public assistance the agency is able to provide in case of disasters such as floods, storms, tornadoes, earthquakes, and other acts of destruction. Your discussion can include the cleanup necessary after the disaster.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: After completing either 7(a)(1) or 7(a)(2), do ALL of the following: (1) Compare the four leading causes of mortality (death) in your community for any of the past five years with the four leading causes of disease in your community. Explain how the public health agency you visited is trying to reduce the mortality and morbidity rates of these leading causes of illness and death. (2) Explain the role of your health agency as it relates to the outbreak of diseases. (3) Discuss the kinds of public assistance the agency is able to provide in case of disasters such as floods, storms, tornadoes, earthquakes, and other acts of destruction. Your discussion can include the cleanup necessary after the disaster.

pamphlet_excerpts: Responsibilities Public: One of the responsibilities of public health professionals is tobecome familiar with diseases, their causes, and their cures tohelp protect.
But Individuals: But individuals also can help maintainpublic health, and their own health, by learning about diseases.
Examples Ofthese Infectious: Some examples ofthese infectious diseases are tetanus (bacterial), influenza andcoronavirus (viral), athlete’s foot (fungal), and hookworm.
Benzene Chemical Tobacco: Benzene, a chemical found in tobacco smoke, vehicleexhaust, detergents, and other sources, can cause leukemia.
step_by_step_procedure: Diseases Passed Genes: Diseases that are passed through the genes, from parents tooffspring, are known as hereditary diseases.
Examples Includesickle-cell: Examples includesickle-cell anemia and hemophilia.
Diseases Caused Poor: Still other diseases may be caused by poor lifestyle choices.
Encouraging Healthydietary: Encouraging healthydietary habits and regular physical activity can markedlyreduce the numbers of deaths from heart attacks each year.

pamphlet_excerpts: Public Health Specialists: Many public health specialists are employed in hospitals, universities, and private industry.
Public Health Officials: Public health officials are employed at all levels of government.
Local Communities: In local communities, sanitarians and health officersensure that establishments handle food safely.
They Enforcelocal: They enforcelocal regulations so that communities can stay safe and healthy.
step_by_step_procedure: Requirements Positions Vary: The requirements for these positions vary from state to state.
Career Sanitarian College: A career sanitarian usually has some college education; healthofficers must have experience and, often, an advanced degreesuch as a masters.
Armed Forceshave: All of the armed forceshave professionals to help maintain the health of their members and prevent injuries.
Internationally Opportunities: Internationally, the opportunities to apply public healthskills are almost unlimited.
